# Klipse

> Klipse (klipse.app) is an AI-powered short-form video creation and auto-publishing SaaS. Users describe a content idea; Klipse generates a complete vertical video — AI script, AI images, AI voiceover, optional AI background sound, FFmpeg-encoded — then publishes it automatically to YouTube (and future platforms) on a configurable schedule. No editing, no rendering, no manual uploading required.

## What Klipse Does

Klipse is a queue-driven AI content pipeline for creators and operators who want to run automated content channels without manual video production. The user provides a channel niche and topic ideas; Klipse handles every production step end-to-end:

1. AI generates a spoken-word script (voiceover text + image prompts + title + description + tags)
2. AI generates matching images (one per script segment)
3. AI generates text-to-speech narration audio
4. Optionally: AI generates ambient background sound/music
5. FFmpeg encodes images + audio into a video (slideshow style)
6. Video is published to the user's connected YouTube channel automatically, or held for manual approval

## Pricing Plans

All paid plans billed monthly via Polar. Credits are consumed at job creation time (not completion). Unused monthly credits do not roll over.

### Free Plan
- Price: $0/month
- Monthly credits: 0 (one free trial video only, no recurring credits)
- Channels: 1 (for onboarding/preview only)
- Video duration cap: 30 seconds
- Publishing: Not available (free tier is generate-and-view only)
- Background sound: Not available
- Schedule fast-forward: Not available
- Watermark: Yes (Klipse watermark overlaid on video)
- One-time trial video with no credit cost; video is temporarily stored and then purged

### Starter Plan
- Price: Paid monthly (see klipse.app/dashboard/billing for current pricing)
- Monthly credits: 1,500
- Channels: 1
- Video duration cap: 30 seconds
- Publishing: Yes (YouTube auto-publish)
- Background sound: Not available
- Schedule fast-forward: Not available (must wait for next scheduled run)
- Destination replacements per billing cycle: 1
- Watermark: No

### Creator Plan
- Price: Paid monthly
- Monthly credits: 5,000
- Channels: 3
- Video duration cap: 60 seconds
- Publishing: Yes (YouTube auto-publish)
- Background sound: Yes (AI-generated via ElevenLabs)
- Schedule fast-forward: Yes (trigger schedule immediately)
- Destination replacements per billing cycle: 5
- Watermark: No

### Empire Plan
- Price: Paid monthly
- Monthly credits: 15,000
- Channels: 20
- Video duration cap: Up to 600 seconds (10 minutes), limited by channel config
- Publishing: Yes (YouTube auto-publish)
- Background sound: Yes (AI-generated via ElevenLabs)
- Schedule fast-forward: Yes
- Destination replacements per billing cycle: 30
- Watermark: No

### Credit Add-ons (One-Time Purchases)
- Small pack: 750 credits
- Large pack: 2,000 credits

## Credit Costs Per Operation

Credits are deducted atomically at job creation. The total cost depends on script length, image count, and TTS character count.

- Script generation: 5 credits (flat)
- Image generation: 2 credits per image
- TTS (text-to-speech): 4 credits per 1,000 characters of voiceover text
- Video assembly (FFmpeg encode): 3 credits (flat)
- AI video (future/alternate pipeline): 3 credits per second of video

A typical 30-second video with 3 images and ~500 TTS characters costs approximately: 5 + 6 + 2 + 3 = 16 credits.

## Video Specifications

- Format: MP4 (H.264 video + AAC audio)
- Aspect ratios supported: 9:16 (portrait, default — YouTube Shorts), 16:9 (landscape), 1:1 (square)
- Duration: Configurable per channel; capped by plan (Free/Starter: 30s, Creator: 60s, Empire: up to 600s)
- Style: Slideshow (AI-generated images + voiceover narration)
- AI disclosure: Added automatically to video metadata (description) per platform guidelines
- Free tier: Watermark ("Klipse") overlaid in center of video

## Channel Configuration

A "channel" in Klipse is a publishing destination with its own identity, niche, and settings. Each channel is independent and produces videos autonomously.

- **Platform**: YouTube (connected via OAuth). TikTok and Instagram are planned.
- **Niche**: A text description of the channel's topic/genre (e.g. "5-minute history facts", "daily finance tips"). Used as context for AI script generation.
- **Name**: Display name of the channel. Used in video metadata and AI prompts.
- **Aspect ratio**: 9:16 (default), 16:9, or 1:1
- **Target duration**: Desired video length in seconds (clamped by plan limit)
- **Sound enabled**: Whether to generate AI background sound (Creator+ only)
- **Sound prompt hint**: Optional text hint to guide background sound generation
- **Publish approval**: Videos can be set to require manual approval before publishing, or auto-publish immediately on completion

## Scheduling

Each channel can have one active schedule. The cron system polls for due schedules approximately every minute.

- **Frequencies**: daily, every 2 days, every 3 days, every 4 days, every 5 days, every 6 days, weekly, every 2 weeks, every 3 weeks, monthly
- **Jitter**: Random offset up to 360 minutes added to each scheduled run time to prevent all channels from firing simultaneously
- **Fast-forward**: Creator+ plans can trigger a schedule to run immediately without waiting for the next scheduled time
- **One-off generation**: Any plan can trigger a manual video generation from the Generate page at any time (consumes credits)

## Publishing Workflow

1. Video job completes encoding
2. If publish approval is set to "pending": job waits for user to approve/reject in dashboard
3. If approved (or auto-approve): Klipse fetches the output MP4 and uploads to YouTube via YouTube Data API v3
4. YouTube returns a video ID; job is marked published
5. If YouTube token is revoked/expired: user receives an email notification to reconnect their channel

**Manual retry**: If publishing fails (e.g. token expired, user has reconnected), there is a "Retry publish" button in the job history.

**Publishing platforms**: Currently YouTube only. TikTok and Instagram are in the schema/roadmap but not yet live.

## Authentication

- **Email OTP**: Enter email → receive 6-digit code → sign in (no password required)
- **Google OAuth**: Sign in with Google account
- Sessions are managed server-side
- Admin accounts can be designated via environment config; admins have access to an admin panel

## Job Lifecycle

Each video generation is tracked as a "job" with the following statuses:

- `queued`: Job created, waiting for cron to pick it up
- `dispatched`: Cron has sent the job to the video processor
- `processing`: Processor is actively running pipeline stages
- `completed`: Video encoded and stored; ready to publish or already published
- `failed`: An error occurred during processing

Pipeline stages (in order):
1. `dispatch_pending` → `script` (LLM script generation)
2. `prepare` (image generation + TTS + optional sound)
3. `assemble` (FFmpeg encode + watermark + R2 upload)
4. `done` (complete)

**Manual retry**: Failed jobs can be manually retried up to 3 times from the job history page.

## AI Technology Stack

- **Script generation**: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (primary) → OpenRouter fallback
- **Image generation**: Replicate SDXL
- **Text-to-speech**: Google Cloud TTS (primary) → Unreal Speech → ElevenLabs (fallback chain)
- **Background sound**: ElevenLabs (Creator+ only)
- **Video encoding**: FFmpeg (runs in external Node.js service on Google Cloud Run)

## Storage & Data

- Final videos stored in Cloudflare R2 (object storage)
- Free tier videos are stored temporarily and purged after a set retention window
- Paid tier videos remain available as long as the job record exists
- Job artifacts include: AI-generated title, description, tags, and script text

## Analytics

Users can view:
- Total completed/failed jobs
- Success rate
- Credits used this month
- Per-channel job counts (completed/failed)
- Daily job completion chart (last 30 days)

## Support & Contact

- Support email: Available in dashboard settings (see VITE_APP_SUPPORT_EMAIL)
- Discord community: Available via dashboard links (see VITE_APP_DISCORD_URL)
- Bug reports: Available via in-app bug report link

## Key Concepts Glossary

- **Credit**: Internal currency consumed per video operation. Resets monthly for paid plans.
- **Channel**: A named publishing destination with its own niche, platform connection, and schedule.
- **Niche**: The topic/genre description that guides AI content generation for a channel.
- **Job**: A single video generation request, tracked from creation through publishing.
- **Pipeline**: The sequence of AI and encoding stages that transform a topic idea into a published video.
- **Publish approval**: A gate where the user manually reviews a completed video before it goes live.
- **Schedule fast-forward**: Triggering a scheduled generation immediately rather than waiting for the next scheduled time (Creator+ feature).
- **Destination replacement**: Switching a channel's connected platform account (e.g. linking to a different YouTube channel). Limited per billing cycle by plan.
- **Watermark**: "Klipse" text overlay on free-tier videos.
- **AI disclosure**: Text added to video descriptions noting AI-generated content.
